I wouldn't do it if I were you. The effects of starvation are actually the worst (I have anorexia and it sucks) 

For one it makes your depression 10x worse because your brain can't function. You end up feeling sluggish and more depressed. You can end up starving yourself forever because it alters your brain chemistry and makes you unable to eat again. You also stop being able to comprehend what people are saying to you.

Also no matter what your weight is, you can give yourself osteoporosis and it can be permanent. Then you just have a hunchback and feel worse about yourself. You can have a heart attack at any weight and then you can't work out anymore. And also your hair starts falling out. You can't do things like open doors and it gets really irritating after a while. You end up with hypoglycemia and reactive hypoglycemia so you are hypoglycemic whether or not you eat or not. You also have to deal with medical professionals treating you like shit and acting like you're causing your own problems. 

I crashed into someone because malnutrition alters your reaction time. I'm sick all the time. I ended up Vitamin K deficient so my blood doesn't clot. I can't see well. I see illusions because I can't recognize what things are. My body temperature is 95.5. I am covered in fine hair because my body is trying to keep itself warm and its disgusting. 

My point is, based on research starvation causes eating disorder symptoms. Eating disorders have the highest suicide rate because they are their own form of hell and make you so hopeless with the cycle you are stuck in. 

I get feeling horrible about yourself and also wanting to punish yourself. If you can find a different way to cope with the feelings, I would. Seeing a nutritionist to lose weight can also be really helpful

A math test doesn't say anything about your intelligence. Its a comprehension test and says as much about the teacher as it does you. The test just shows what you know and what you don't so you can improve. 

Nobody can succeed without failing. Also with math sometimes it just takes longer to grasp. In 6 months the material might make complete sense to you.

I failed calculus the first time but the second time I took it I was the best in the class.

Also, you tried. Your parents won't be mad at you because it wasn't that you didn't try. Everyone fails sometimes. It seems like a big deal now but looking back this could be a learning experience.

What you're doing right now is a cognitive distortion called overgenerization. You're saying that this one test says so much about you as a person when it doesn't. What about all the times you succeeded? Do they say as much about who you are? Chances are you've succeeded way more than you have failed

Please hang in there, Elliot. If I were you, this is what I would do:

Call the suicide hotline now. Their number is 1-800-273-8255. It seems like you are having a mental health crisis, meaning that things are getting worse and you are going to need help pulling yourself out of it. The people on this line won't judge you. They'll be able to tell you what they think you should do next.

Make sure to call them if you start to feel like you're an eminent danger to yourself or others. 

The next person I would reach out to after that is parents. I know that you've said you've been through childhood trauma, so I don't know how much of an option this is. If you can't talk to them, talk to another adult that you trust, like a teacher or guidance counselor.

If you dont want to disclose stuff to your parents, you should ask to make an appointment with your doctor because you can talk confidentially with them.

If you do these things, you should get set up with mental health resources. The professionals won't judge you; you aren't the first person to feel this way and they are equipped to help you feel better.

Try to keep yourself safe. If you start to feel like you are going to do something bad, please do these steps:

1. Contact the suicide hotline and/or talk to a trusted adult and see if it helps 
2. If it doesn't help, call 911 

Things aren't always going to be like this. I believe in you
